skill.name: product-design-harness
skill.description: Review product decisions across user needs, evidence quality, and business viability before design, implementation, launch, or scaling.
skill.summary: Turn product assumptions into structured reviews, focused verification steps, and bounded implementation handoffs.
skill.author: cis2042

content.value_statement: Product teams can build quickly while important assumptions remain untested. This skill structures user, evidence, and business reviews into clear decisions and bounded next steps.
actual_capabilities: Select Quick Gate, Standard Gate, or UX3 Council based on scope, uncertainty, risk, and reversibility.
Review user needs, evidence strength, and business viability independently before combining their verdicts.
Produce continue, verify, or stop_reframe decisions using the worst lane verdict and a deterministic weakest-flow rule.
Define implementation boundaries, proof steps, stop conditions, and human approval requirements.
Validate review artifacts and matching context packs with bundled Python helpers.
Guide council challenge rounds, claim analysis, evidence receipts, and accountable human decision records.
limitations: The skill does not generate real customer evidence or replace direct research.
Schema validation checks structure and selected rules, not evidence truth or decision quality.
Human approvals and execution restrictions require enforcement by the host runtime or team.
Local validation requires Python and the declared jsonschema dependency; agent registration and CI integration require separate setup.

use_cases.title: Evaluate a Feature Before Development
use_cases.description: Review demand, current workarounds, evidence gaps, and business costs before committing engineering capacity.

use_cases.title: Test a Risky Design Assumption
use_cases.description: Identify affected people, interaction burdens, and disconfirming tests before expanding a prototype.

use_cases.title: Bound an Agent Implementation Handoff
use_cases.description: Create a reviewed context pack with explicit scope, prohibited actions, approval gates, and stop conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Review Mode
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this product idea: [idea]. Do not implement. Select the smallest responsible mode, explain why, and list missing intake and evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: Start with an incomplete product idea.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Standard Feature Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a Standard Gate for [feature] using [evidence]. Review user, evidence, and business flows independently. Return the weakest flow, verdict, and bounded next action.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: Evaluate a proposed feature before development.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Bounded Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [validated continue review] to create a matching context pack. Preserve scope, prohibitions, human gates, evidence references, and stop conditions. Validate both artifacts together.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: Prepare reviewed work for implementation without expanding permissions.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a High-Risk Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Run UX3 Council for [decision] using [claims and evidence]. Include independent lanes, challenge rounds, uncertainty review, and required red-team analysis. Validate the final result.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: Evaluate a consequential decision with multiple stakeholders.

output_examples.input: Managers requested weekly report exports, but no behavior data supports building scheduled delivery.
output: Next step: Test a static report sample during five workflow interviews.
Boundary: Do not build scheduled exports, access live customer data, or change permissions.
Stop condition: Managers cannot identify a recurring decision that the report supports.

output_examples.input: A team proposes an automation feature for everyone, based only on internal enthusiasm.
output: Missing intake: A specific operator, affected people, current workaround, issuer, and accountable owner.
Reframed question: Which specific workflow has an observed cost that automation could reduce?
Boundary: Define the research question before implementation.

output_examples.input: A validated continue review permits one reversible prototype and excludes production changes.
output: Handoff: Create a context pack matching the reviewed boundary.
Allowed work: Build the specified prototype and evaluate its acceptance criteria.
Prohibited work: Production deployment, scope expansion, and unapproved data access.
Approval: Preserve every human gate from the review.
Stop condition: Pause when affected people, data, risk, or scope changes.

best_practices: Supply traceable evidence, affected stakeholders, an issuer, and an accountable owner before requesting a handoff.
Validate every completed review and context pack together before acting on their boundaries.
Keep proof steps small and preserve human approval gates when work moves between agents.
anti_patterns: Treating simulated users, opinions, or model confidence as verified behavioral evidence.
Averaging reviewer verdicts to hide a blocking lane.
Turning a verify decision into general implementation or expanding a context pack without review.

faq.question: Does this skill build the product?
faq.answer: Its primary role is review and handoff preparation. Implementation follows a continue verdict, a validated context pack, and any required human approvals.

faq.question: Which review modes are available?
faq.answer: Quick Gate covers small reversible changes. Standard Gate covers new features or workflows. UX3 Council handles high uncertainty, risk, or human-owned trade-offs.

faq.question: What happens when evidence is weak?
faq.answer: The review returns verify or stop_reframe. Missing traceable evidence blocks continuation, while isolated opinions can support at most verification.

faq.question: Does the helper contact external services?
faq.answer: The bundled helpers read local artifacts and schemas. They do not make model API calls or automatically retrieve customer evidence.

faq.question: Can a validated context pack replace human approval?
faq.answer: No. Validation preserves listed human gates; it does not grant them. The host runtime or team must enforce approval requirements.

faq.question: What is required to run validation?
faq.answer: Use Python with the declared jsonschema dependency. Run the bundled review checker on the review and its context pack before handoff.
